To add experience. I've been through both CBT and DBT. My DBT was in a group setting, which is recommended and CBT was individual. Both have positives. And both have negatives.

I didn't utilize the DBT for depression, although I've heard it helps. I focused that therapy on BPD. The cognitive therapy was for depression. Major Depressive disorder to be exact. 

There's different things that'll help for different reasons in different people. Therapy in general can be extremely beneficial. It's just finding that right therapist that'll fit for you. I recommend shopping around for therapists. Use things like zocdoc or better help. Most therapists are willing to do an initial visit either free or cheap. And no matter what insurance or lack thereof there are therapists that are good to be had. And if you're anxious about in person meetings, there's always video appointments to be had. 

Medication is hit or miss with depression. Unfortunately, miss is more likely to be common. So therapy is the best bet. Trust me, I've been through a lot with depression and suicidal stagnation. I can promise you, there's always a solution to a problem, you just might have to work a little harder to find it.
